title: Workspace: should every extension-types crate carrying a content hash on the wire depend on jmap-cid-types?
description:
Surfaced by bd:JMAP-ly0n.20. Attachment.sha256 in jmap-chat-types is currently String with a stale rationale doc-comment. The bead recommended switching to jmap_cid_types::Sha256.

This is a workspace-architectural decision the agent does not have authorization to make autonomously:

1. The per-crate AGENTS.md for jmap-chat-types lists only {jmap-types, serde, serde_json} as allowed deps and explicitly says 'Do not introduce a dependency that jmap-mail-types does not also have, without explicit user approval.'

2. jmap-mail-types (the workspace-canonical extension-types crate) also does not depend on jmap-cid-types, even though Email/EmailBodyPart carries blob_id which is the field the workspace AGENTS.md cites jmap-cid-types as the canonical home for ('feeds Blob upload responses and FileNode objects in a future jmap-base-client / jmap-filenode-types revision').

The question: should the canonical (jmap-mail-types) take a hard dep on jmap-cid-types as the first step in a workspace-wide propagation, after which every extension-types sibling that carries a content hash on the wire (Attachment.sha256 in chat-types, future FileNode-style hashes in filenode-types, etc.) follows?

Options:
- (A) Propagate jmap-cid-types into the extension-types family canonical-first, starting with jmap-mail-types. Touches the per-crate AGENTS.md dep policies (workspace-wide amendment).
- (B) Keep jmap-cid-types as a standalone wire-shape crate consumed only by jmap-base-client and the (future) jmap-filenode-types. Extension-types crates that happen to carry content hashes keep them as String with consumer-side validation. The Attachment.sha256 doc-comment refresh in bd:JMAP-ly0n.20 reflects this option.
- (C) Some narrower scope (e.g. only chat-types takes the dep because it has an explicit Attachment.sha256 wire field that no other current extension carries).

Recommendation: option (A) is the cleanest design but is a workspace-wide change that should be planned, not done one-off. Option (B) is the lowest-energy answer and is what bd:JMAP-ly0n.20 landed pending this decision. Option (C) is a divergence from the canonical-template rule and is least preferred.

Until this is resolved, the bd:JMAP-ly0n.20 doc-comment refresh is the documented posture; any consumer that needs a typed sha256 can use jmap_cid_types::Sha256 themselves via a TryFrom<&str> at their boundary.
notes: Folded into JMAP-01ba (CID FileNode extension and CIDv1 (draft-atwood-jmap-cid-00)) by the 2026-10-19 spec gap audit.
